english.title: Knowingly cause / permit setting of electrical device or substance to injure Schedule 6 wild animal - England
english.standardoffencewording:
On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..), knowingly caused or permitted the setting of

(A)_[an electrical device for killing or stunning]_
(B)_[a poisonous, poisoned or stupefying substance]_

of such a nature and so placed in England as to be calculated to cause bodily injury to a wild animal included in Schedule 6 to the Wildlife and Countryside Act 1981
english.legislation: Contrary to sections 11(2)(c)(i), 11(2)(f) and 21(1) of the Wildlife and Countryside Act 1981.

english.notes:
(i) Section 47 of the Agriculture (Wales) Act 2023 in force from the 17th October 2023 distinguished the prohibitions on the killing or taking of animals in England and Wales so different obligations apply in each geographic region. This offence applies to England only. For the offence applying in Wales, see H101449. For the offence applying in England/Wales before the 17th October 2023, see H20037.
(ii) See section 21(7) of the Wildlife and Countryside Act 1981 for place where offence deemed to have been committed for jurisdiction purposes.
(iii) See section 11(5) for presumption that animal is wild and section 27 for meaning of "wild animal".
(iv) See section 21(6) for the forfeiture provisions.
(v) See section 11(7) for defence.

other.penalty:
Summary: maximum 6 months imprisonment and / or a fine.

Where more than one animal is involved in a single offence the maximum fine shall be determined as if the person convicted had been convicted of a separate offence in respect of each animal (section 21(5)).

Time limit for prosecutions:
Complex, see section 20 of the Wildlife and Countryside Act 1981.
